name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 365 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 21% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 365 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 21 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces in Manipur arrested two NRFM cadres, seized 7.7 kg of brown sugar and a cache of weapons, while the Assam Rifles DG reviewed border fencing and joint grids in Moreh. A woman was killed and three injured when a tempo rolled down a road in Reasi, and a man was injured in a bear attack in South Kashmir. Cyclone Arnab killed six people on India’s eastern coast and former Maoist commanders married in Hazaribagh open jail as police intervened. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Manipur arresterte to NRFM-medlemmer, beslagla 7.7 kg brunt sukker og en våpenbeholdning, mens DG for Assam Rifles gjennomgikk grensegjerdet og felles gittere i Moreh. En kvinne ble drept og tre ble såret da et tempo rullet nedover en vei i Reasi, og en mann ble skadet i et bjørneangrep i Sør-Kashmir. Syklon Arnab drepte seks personer på Indias østkyst, og tidligere maoistkommandanter giftet seg i Hazaribagh åpne fengsel mens politiet greide inn. 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
